thought.text: The orchestrator is running (2 demospipes bases succeeded). Let me diagnose the other failures in detail:

reasoning_content:
Two distinct problems:
1. **`[tool.uv.audit]` unknown field** — The uv 0.9.30 in the container doesn't recognize the `[tool.uv.audit]` table that exists in several pyproject.toml files. This is in the source repo (it was there from the start, e.g., demospipes/core has `[tool.uv.audit]`). Wait — but demospipes-base-api and base-executors built fine with rc=0 even though their pyproject.toml has `[tool.uv.audit]`. Why? Because those Dockerfiles use `pip wheel` instead of `uv sync` for the build! The `test-deps` stage uses `uv sync --locked`, which… wait, did it succeed? Let me check: demospipes-base-api rc=0. Its Dockerfile's test-deps stage runs `uv sync --locked --group dev --group test`. And it succeeded. Hmm, but core also has `[tool.uv.audit]`. So why does uv 0.9.30 not error on demospipes/core but does error on dokumentensuche?

Wait — let me check the uv version. Container ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.12-bookworm reports `uv 0.9.30`. And demospipes-base-api succeeded with `uv sync --locked` in a pyproject containing `[tool.uv.audit]`. Contradictory… unless `uv sync --locked` skips full TOML validation when it can use the lockfile as-is? No — the TOML parse error should occur either way when reading the workspace.

Hmm, wait, maybe demospipes-base-api's lockfile was regenerated by my host-side uv 0.13.1 and… the error is a TOML "parse error" — an unknown field in a `[tool.uv.audit]` table. That error occurs when uv parses the pyproject. demospipes/core has:
```
[tool.uv.audit]
ignore = []
```
Let me check which services' pyprojects contain `[tool.uv.audit]` in /workspace (not stage): dokumentenaufbereitung-monorepo, dokumentensuche, dokumentenaufbereitung-data-service, nachforderungen, dokumentenschwaerzung-pdf-pii-detector, demospipes/{data-structures,core,api}.

demospipes's api/core have it but built successfully?! Let me look at those logs… maybe uv 0.9.30 only errors on unknown fields when it needs to resolve (uv lock/sync without --frozen?)… no, that's not it. Or — demospipes-base-api's `uv sync --locked --group dev --group test`: hmm.

Wait, maybe I misread: the error message "unknown field `audit`" lists expected fields — that's uv 0.9.30's schema. But maybe demospipes's `[tool.uv.audit]` is… let me check if uv sync with `--locked` bypasses the pyproject's tool.uv section? No, that's not it either.

Let me actually check the demospipes-base-api log and see if uv sync ran and succeeded, or if the test-deps stage got skipped/failed silently. rc=0 means the whole build succeeded, so the test-deps stage including `uv sync --locked --group dev --group test` did succeed with a pyproject containing [tool.uv.audit].

Interesting. So why does the same thing fail for dokumentensuche? Difference: uv sync without `--locked`? No wait — dokumentensuche's Dockerfile: `uv sync --no-cache --no-dev` (no --locked!). When --locked is not specified, uv needs to… still read pyproject's tool.uv. Hmm.

Actually — I think the difference is this: `uv sync --locked` reads the lockfile and validates it against pyproject. In that flow, it parses the `[tool.uv]` section… apparently tolerating unknown sub-tables? No…

Hmm, actually maybe: uv 0.9.30's strict TOML validation on `tool.uv` only applies when it needs to resolve dependencies (i.e., when the lock is missing/invalid or when resolving is needed). With `--locked` and a valid lock, no resolution happens and unknown fields are ignored?? That's plausible: the config parser uses a `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` schema for resolution settings… but if it parses the entire tool.uv table eagerly, it should fail either way.

Let me look at this from a different angle: which failing services ran `uv sync --locked`?
- berichtskonfigurator: `uv sync --locked --no-install-project --no-dev` → failed on editable metadata (bizlog path issue? no — "Failed to generate package metadata for berichtskonfigurator-backend @ editable+." — because `COPY pyproject.toml` happened but `COPY ./src ./src` … wait, that's in the builder stage; the failure line shows `uv sync --locked --no-install-project --no-dev` on line 22 of the Dockerfile. The error is generating the project's own editable metadata. Why? Because it can't parse bizlog's path? Earlier log (first run) showed "Failed to parse entry: `bizlog` — path could not be normalized: /app/../../03-shared-services/bizlog". In the new run, the error is simply "Failed to generate package metadata for `berichtskonfigurator-backend==0.37.0 @ editable+.`" — I need to check the cause line.
- dokumentenpruefung: `Distribution not found at: file:///app/bizlog` — bizlog was found by name but the directory isn't at /app/bizlog?? The rewriter labeled it `path = "bizlog"` (relative to the service root, where bizlog/ is already copied). But the Dockerfile's first uv sync runs before `COPY . /app`? No — dokumentenpruefung's Dockerfile does `COPY . /app` first, then uv sync. Hmm wait, the new log says `file:///app/bizlog` not found. So at the point of uv sync, /app/bizlog didn't exist. In dokumentenpruefung's Dockerfile: WORKDIR /app; COPY . /app; then uv sync. If COPY . /app succeeded, bizlog/ should be there… unless .dockerignore is excluding it! dokumentenpruefung's .dockerignore — I saw the full contents earlier: it has `.venv/`, `*.env`, `!*.env.example`, and… let me check if it's excluding something relevant. Actually, I didn't see it excluding bizlog. Hmm.

Wait, actually — maybe the issue is: the stage directory $d has service files at the root and dependency directories alongside them. `COPY . /app` copies everything including the bizlog/ directory. So /app/bizlog should exist. Unless .dockerignore has a pattern like `lib/`… no. Hmm, but "Distribution not found at file:///app/bizlog" — bizlog's pyproject is at /app/bizlog/pyproject.toml. Let me check what's actually in the staged dokumentenpruefung and what .dockerignore excludes.

Actually wait — dokumentenpruefung's .dockerignore: from the earlier output, it contained standard stuff + `audit_sequence.json` etc. Did it exclude `bizlog`? No. But maybe there's a generic pattern… I need to check for real.

And "Failed to generate package metadata for X @ editable+." in the first stage (test-deps) — for berichtskonfigurator, the test-deps stage runs before the src copy? Let me look at berichtskonfigurator's Dockerfile in full: lines 12–27: WORKDIR /app, COPY ./src ./src, COPY pyproject.toml, README.md, uv.lock, then `uv sync --locked --no-install-project --no-dev` — hmm wait, that grep showed line 16 COPY ./src, line 18 pyproject, line 19 README, line 20 uv.lock, line 27 uv sync. So src is already copied. So why does the editable metadata fail? Cause: the project has a path dependency on bizlog etc., and uv reads the project's pyproject [tool.uv.sources] → the path is currently "bizlog" → /app/bizlog doesn't exist (only src/ and manifests have been copied so far!). That's it! In the first stage, only the service's own files are copied — the staged dependency directories (bizlog/) are at the context root, but the Dockerfile only copies specific things (./src, pyproject.toml, uv.lock) and not the sibling dep directories!

So for services that only COPY specific files in the first stage, my staging (putting deps as sibling directories at the context root) is useless — the Dockerfile has to copy them. The bind mount + `--no-install-project` flow: `uv sync --locked --no-install-project` still needs to read the project's [tool.uv.sources] to build the project graph?? It does — the error indicates it's trying to generate the project's own editable metadata even with --no-install-project (to build the graph).

Options:
A. Modify the staged Dockerfile to also COPY the dependency directories before uv sync. E.g., insert `COPY bizlog/ bizlog/` etc. before each uv sync in the staged Dockerfile. This means editing the Dockerfile per service — possible via a general patcher: for each external dependency directory name D (which is in the context and needed), if the Dockerfile has `COPY . /app` (full copy), the deps come along automatically — no problem. Only services with selective COPY need patching: which ones? Let me enumerate: from the earlier survey, services that COPY . /app: decision-log-store-service, demos-einwendungsmanagement, dokumentenpruefung, fristenmanagement, graph-api, ki-guv-*, kommentar-service, nachforderungen, ner-extraction, norm-matching, rechtsquellenvorbereitung, request-proxy, risikohinweis, subsumtion, xoev-adapter, demospipes api/core, bmds addons (copying subdirectories). Services with selective COPY: berichtskonfigurator (COPY ./src, pyproject, uv.lock, tests, scripts), dokumentensuche (COPY pyproject uv.lock; src/; config/), dokumentenaufbereitung-data-service (COPY pyproject uv.lock; then COPY . .), dokumentenschwaerzung-orchestrator (first COPY . ., then COPY pyproject uv.lock — order?), pdf-pii-detector (COPY pyproject uv.lock; then COPY . .), tex2pdf (selective), ki-validierung (COPY uv.lock pyproject; then COPY .).

Wait, but dokumentenpruefung uses full `COPY . /app` — so /app/bizlog should exist. Its error: "Distribution not found at: file:///app/bizlog". Hmm! Why? Let me check the context: stage dir /workspace/.build-logs/stage/dokumentenpruefung has bizlog/ at the top (from my earlier test, yes). So COPY . /app → /app/bizlog. It should be there… unless .dockerignore is excluding it! dokumentenpruefung's .dockerignore — let me look at it fully. I saw it earlier; it contained things like `sandbox/*`. Hmm, was there a `*.egg-info`? Yes, but that's unrelated.

Oh, wait. I think I get it. In the new orchestrator run, the stage for dokumentenpruefung was rebuilt by stage_and_queue — rsync copied the service, then dependencies, then the rewriter + relock. Did the rewriter relabel correctly? relock.log said "rewrote 20 paths" total for the whole run… let me check the stage dir directly. Also, check if the log shows which stage failed: the log line shows `RUN ... uv sync --no-cache --no-dev`?? For dokumentensuche, yes. Let me look at the exact failing command + stage for dokumentenpruefung.

Let me debug concretely: inspect the current stage/dokumentenpruefung (does bizlog/ exist? what are the path values in the pyproject?) and the log context.

2. **`[tool.uv.audit]` unknown field in uv 0.9.30** — affects dokumentenaufbereitung-data-service, -monorepo, dokumentensuche, dokumentenschwaerzung-pdf-pii-detector, nachforderungen. Solution: patch the staged pyproject to remove the `[tool.uv.audit]` table (host-side, in the staging step) — this is audit configuration and not needed for the build. Or, upgrade the container's uv to 0.13.1 (matching host). The latter is cleaner and also avoids other schema mismatches between lockfile version and container's uv! Lockfiles generated by uv 0.13.1 might have a newer lockfile format that 0.9.30 can't read → `uv sync --locked` will fail with "lockfile needs updating". But demospipes-base-api succeeded with host-generated lock + container's uv 0.9.30… so lockfile format is compatible (uv maintains backward compat for one minor version… whatever, it worked).

Regarding [tool.uv.audit]: does it exist in the original repo? Yes (demospipes/core has it, and it built fine!). So why did it build fine?! Its test-deps stage ran `uv sync --locked --group dev --group test` with uv 0.9.30 and [tool.uv.audit] in pyproject → success. So uv 0.9.30 doesn't reject tool.uv.audit in that flow… but for dokumentensuche (`uv sync --no-cache --no-dev` — no --locked) it did reject. So: uv 0.9.30 only strictly validates [tool.uv] when it needs to perform a resolve (lockfile missing/stale, or no --locked → refresh resolution). With --locked + valid lock, no resolve → the config is parsed leniently? Actually more likely: uv parses tool.uv config only when needed for resolution; `--locked` skips resolution entirely and reads the lockfile as-is.

Hmm wait, but my host-side relock (uv 0.13.1) regenerated all uv.lock files. For services where the Dockerfile runs `uv sync --locked` — the lock exists and matches pyproject → no problem. But for the stage relock — I ran `uv lock` (13.1). If the container's uv 0.9.30 sees a lockfile in version "1.1" (or whatever 13.1 emits) vs the expected "1.0" → error "The lockfile at `uv.lock` was created by uv 0.13.1 and is not compatible with this version (0.9.30)"? If that were happening, demospipes-base-api would have failed. It didn't. Let me check what lockfile version my uv 0.13.1 wrote, and whether there's an upgrade note in the demospipes-base-api log.

The simplest, most robust fix for both issues: **upgrade the container's uv to the same version (0.13.1) inside the staged Dockerfile**. But that requires a Dockerfile edit (RUN uv tool install… no — `uv self update`? uv image: is the `uv` binary at /usr/local/bin/uv? In the ghcr uv image, uv is installed via the official installer to /root/.local/bin or /usr/local/bin. `uv self update` works in the official image (it's installed as standalone, not via cargo). Add `RUN uv self update` at the top? Network needed during build — that's fine (PyPI/ghcr worked; does uv self update from GitHub releases? Downloads from https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases — reachable).

Hmm, but wait — is [tool.uv.audit] really in the repo, or did I add it?? No — I haven't edited any pyproject in /workspace at all, except via the stage. Let me check the original: /workspace/02-backend/dokumentensuche/pyproject.toml — my earlier grep listed it under tool.uv.audit, yes. And demospipes/core also has it. But demospipes-base-api succeeded… its pyproject (api) has [tool.uv.audit] per the grep list. So the successful build proves that 0.9.30 + [tool.uv.audit] + `uv sync --locked` works.

And the failing services: dokumentenaufbereitung-data-service (uv sync --no-cache --dev → resolves → strict parse → audit field error). dokumentensuche (uv sync --no-cache --no-dev → resolves (no lock → my lock exists! but no --locked flag → uv sync without --locked still reads the lock… but if the pyproject is "newer" or the lock doesn't match, it may update the lock → resolve → strict parse).

So the minimal, robust fix: **remove the `[tool.uv.audit]` table from the staged pyproject** (it's lint/audit config, irrelevant to the build). Or upgrade uv in the container. Let me go with removing [tool.uv.audit] in staging (deterministic, no network dependency). But if uv 0.9.30 doesn't know about other new fields too (e.g., constraint-dependencies is known in 0.9? [tool.uv] constraint-dependencies has existed since 0.5; ner-extraction uses it — ner-extraction's Dockerfile is `uv sync --no-cache --dev` → resolves → parses tool.uv strictly → is constraint-dependencies known in 0.9.30? Yes, constraint-dependencies has been around since uv 0.4.x). OK.

Actually — a simpler, more global idea: **upgrade the container's uv in the staged Dockerfile**. This would also guarantee lockfile compatibility across all services (0.9.30 vs 0.13.1 lock). But demospipes-base-api already proved that 0.9.30 can read my 0.13.1 lock. Hmm wait, was that really the case? The stage relock of demospipes-base-api was done by host's uv 0.13.1, and the container's 0.9.30 synced --locked successfully. Yes, it proved it.

But there's a subtlety: uv 0.9.30's `uv sync --locked` might accept the lock, but if it needs to parse [tool.uv] for anything (e.g., reading [tool.uv.sources] to install directory deps!) it hits the strict schema → fails even with --locked. In demospipes-base-api, the project has no path deps → [tool.uv.sources] is empty → no issue. For services with path deps + [tool.uv.audit] + `uv sync --locked`: does it parse tool.uv strictly? demospipes-base-executors has a path dep (data-structures) and [tool.uv.audit], and its test-deps ran `uv sync --locked --group dev --group test` → rc=0! So it did parse [tool.uv.sources] (to install the directory dep) without tripping on [tool.uv.audit]??

Confusing. The difference in dokumentensuche's failure is: its command is `uv sync --no-cache --no-dev` (no --locked). Without --locked, uv sync performs an implicit lock refresh: full resolution → strict tool.uv parse → [tool.uv.audit] unknown → dies.

So the rule: services whose uv sync command includes --locked or --frozen skip the strict parse (they can use a valid lock). Services without a lock flag (plain `uv sync`) refresh the lock → strict parse → [tool.uv.audit] error.

Which services run uv sync without a lock flag? From the survey:
- dokumentenaufbereitung-data-service: `uv sync --no-cache --dev --no-install-project` (twice) + `uv sync --no-cache --no-dev` — no --locked.
- dokumentenschwaerzung-orchestrator: `uv sync --no-cache --dev` etc. — no --locked.
- dokumentenschwaerzung-pdf-pii-detector: no --locked.
- dokumentensuche: no --locked.
- ner-extraction: no --locked.
- nachforderungen: `uv sync --no-cache` no lock.
- kommentar-service: `uv sync --frozen` ✓ (frozen = locked).
- tex2pdf: `--frozen` ✓.
- ki-validierung: `--frozen` ✓.

Do orchestrator/pii-detector/ner-extraction/nachforderungen have [tool.uv.audit]? From the grep list: monorepo, dokumentensuche, data-service, nachforderungen, pii-detector (yes); ner-extraction (not in list); dokumentenschwaerzung-orchestrator (not in list). But orchestrator failed with "bizlog not found" (path issue), not audit.

So the plan:
1. In staging, remove the `[tool.uv.audit]` table from all pyproject.toml (harmless for all).
2. Fix the "Distribution not found at /app/<dep>" issue in services that do selective COPY: patch the staged Dockerfile to COPY the dependency directories before the uv sync that needs them. General approach: for each external dependency directory D staged in the context root, ensure it's present in the container at the path that uv expects. uv expects the path relative to the pyproject location in the container. For root-level services: /app/<dep>.

   Per-service approach: after staging, for each dep directory name D:
   - If the Dockerfile has a full `COPY . /app` (or `COPY . .`) before the first uv sync → OK (deps are included) — but the first uv sync must be after that COPY (order matters!).
   - Otherwise, insert `COPY <D>/ <D>/` (or /app/<D>/ depending on WORKDIR) before the first RUN containing `uv sync`.

   Cases:
   - dokumentenpruefung: full `COPY . /app` before uv sync → but the log says /app/bizlog not found?! So something else: .dockerignore is excluding bizlog/! Let me check dokumentenpruefung's .dockerignore for a pattern matching "bizlog"… I don't recall seeing one. Hmm, wait — maybe the issue is different: the log line said `file:///app/bizlog` — that was in the test-deps stage (first stage). dokumentenpruefung's test-deps: COPY . /app (line 23) then uv sync --locked --no-install-project --dev. So /app/bizlog should exist…

   Wait. The stage directory for dokumentenpruefung in this run — did the orchestrator actually stage the deps? services.tsv has 6 deps listed. stage_and_queue rsyncs them. But — a bug: `rsync -a ... "$ROOT/$dep/" "$d/$(basename "$dep")/"` — no issue. Then the rewriter… then the build. So bizlog should be in the context. Unless .dockerignore has `**/bizlog`?? No. Let me just look at the staged directory and the Dockerfile build context. Actually — ah. The context is $d and its .dockerignore is the service's own (rsync copied .dockerignore). dokumentenpruefung's .dockerignore — let me look at it now in full. I have a vague recollection of seeing `.env`, `*.env`, `!*.env.example`… and maybe something like `bizlog`? Unlikely. Let me check.

Actually, hold on — let me reconsider: "Distribution not found at: file:///app/bizlog" — in the new run, the rewriter labeled the root pyproject's bizlog source as `path = "bizlog"`. uv resolves relative to the pyproject's directory = /app. /app/bizlog — needs the bizlog/ directory to be in the context root. It should be there. Unless the rsync in this run didn't happen (stale stage?) — I did `rm -rf .build-logs/stage` before launch, so no.

Let me actually inspect the current stage/dokumentenpruefung to see what's there. And check its .dockerignore too.

Let me pause the orchestrator (it's still running wave A!) and investigate. Actually, let it keep going in the background and debug the stages directly.

3. Also, for demospipes-base-executors's `uv sync --locked --group dev --group test` — the data-structures directory is staged; its Dockerfile first runs `COPY . /app` → /app/data-structures exists ✓ (it succeeded).

Also to double-check: the rewriter only handled pyproject.toml files; the lockfile (uv.lock) contains `source = { directory = "bizlog" }` — after relock, no problem.

But there's another class: services where the uv sync with a lock happens before the full COPY, and the project has no path deps (request-proxy? has bizlog… fristenmanagement? no deps? xoev-adapter? no path deps — OK).

Let me enumerate each service's Dockerfile COPY order + path deps to build the exact patch list. Then patch the staged Dockerfile in the orchestrator:
- For each external dependency directory D, insert `COPY <D> /app/<D>` before the first `RUN ... uv sync` line (for WORKDIR /app) — but careful: in multi-stage, each stage that runs uv sync needs the dep directories. Simplest: insert before every RUN containing `uv sync`? No — the COPY must come after the WORKDIR /app and before the RUN. And `COPY . /app` after an explicit dep COPY is harmless (overwrites with same content… wait, `COPY . /app` copies the context (including D/) into /app — same thing).

Hmm, but a simpler and more robust alternative: **instead of a per-service Dockerfile patch, make the dep available via a different mechanism**: the lockfile's path is `path = "bizlog"` relative to /app — the directory must physically be at /app/bizlog during that RUN. So a COPY is needed.

A cleaner global approach: for each staged service, post-process the Dockerfile:
- Find all external dependency directory names D (from services.tsv).
- For each occurrence of a RUN line containing `uv sync` (a single line in these Dockerfiles — the RUN uses line continuations, but the `uv sync` text is on its own line), insert a `COPY D/ D/` line before the RUN block (i.e., before the RUN keyword line) — but only if there isn't already a preceding full `COPY . ...` after the last FROM in the same stage… actually, just always insert the dep COPY immediately before the RUN line. Even if a full COPY . /app is already before it, an extra COPY D/ D/ is harmless (a no-op content-wise).

Wait, but the RUN block spans multiple lines with backslashes. I need to insert before the `RUN` keyword line itself. Dockerfile parsing: insert `COPY bizlog/ bizlog/` right before the line that starts (after leading whitespace) with `RUN`. That places the COPY after the WORKDIR line (which precedes it) — good. Multiple deps → multiple COPY lines.

Edge cases: demospipes base-executors/api (already OK), bmds addons (their uv sync is in test-deps, COPY api/ → /app — wait, bmds-api's Dockerfile: `COPY api/ /app`, then uv sync --locked --dev in /app. Its pyproject is at /app (api/pyproject.toml copied to /app/pyproject.toml via `COPY api/ /app`). Path deps: `path = "../data-structures"` → after rewriter → the target is external → relabeled to `data-structures`? Wait, bmds-api's deps: demospipes-data-structures (path ../../../data-structures) and demospipes-addon-bmds-data-structures (path ../data_structures). In the stage directory: data-structures/ and data_structures/ are at the root (I staged both). Root pyproject = api/pyproject.toml (the stage root IS the api directory itself — because svcdir = addons/bmds/api, so stage root == api contents: pyproject.toml + demospipes_addon_bmds_api/ + tests/). Dep directories at stage root: data-structures/, data_structures/. The rewriter: S='.' → target '../data-structures' → outside → relabel to 'data-structures'. ✓. In-container: /app/data-structures is needed → insert `COPY data-structures/ data-structures/` + `COPY data_structures/ data_structures/` before the uv sync RUN. But the test-deps stage also needs the pyproject's path deps readable — yes, same fix. But the bmds Dockerfile's `pip wheel` stage: `COPY ./api/pyproject.toml` — no wait, the staged bmds-api Dockerfile still references `COPY api/ /app` and `COPY ./api/pyproject.toml` — because the original context is addons/bmds/ (the parent)! The addon Dockerfile expects the build context to be the addons/bmds/ directory (containing api/, executors/, data_structures/ subdirs)! I staged the contents of api/ at the stage root — that's wrong for the bmds addon Dockerfiles!

Ugh. The bmds addon Dockerfiles use `COPY api/ ...` and `COPY executors/ ...` → they need context = addons/bmds/. So for these two, the stage directory should contain api/, executors/, data_structures/ as subdirectories (i.e., copy the contents of addons/bmds/, not the contents of api/). Then:
- test-deps: COPY api/ /app; uv sync in /app (pyproject=api/pyproject.toml → /app/pyproject.toml), path deps ../data-structures → /data-structures?? No: /app/../data-structures = /data-structures — outside the container FS root → breaks! So the rewriter must label it to a resolvable path: if the deps are staged at context root (data-structures/), then /app/../data-structures doesn't work; but `COPY data-structures/ data-structures/`… hmm, /data-structures (container root) is actually writable (root stage, USER root). COPY data-structures/ /data-structures/ → then the original path `../data-structures` from /app → /data-structures works without a rewriter!! Ha. But my rewriter would relabel it to `data-structures` (relative to S='.') → /app/data-structures — then I'd also need to COPY data-structures/ data-structures/ (into /app). Either way is fine.

But the rewriter also runs `uv lock` in the stage root for bmds services — the stage root has no pyproject (root has api/, executors/, data_structures/ subdirs) → the orchestrator's condition `[ -f "$d/pyproject.toml" ] || ls "$d"/*/pyproject.toml` is true (api/pyproject.toml exists) → rewriter walks all pyprojects and relabels (api, executors, data_structures) — data-structures's pyproject has no path deps; data_structures's pyproject — none. Then `uv lock` in the stage root → no root pyproject → uv lock fails (no project)! → NOLOCK. The lock is in api/uv.lock, executors/uv.lock (from the repo's root stage — did I lock those subprojects at the repo root earlier? Yes: I locked 02-backend/demospipes/addons/bmds/api etc. in the first lock pass — those uv.lock files are in the repo, so they're staged). After the rewriter relabels the paths in api/pyproject.toml, api/uv.lock (old, with ../data-structures) is STALE → `uv sync --locked` in the container fails (lock mismatch)! I must relock per subproject: run uv lock in $d/api and $d/executors.

So the bmds addon staging needs special handling:
- Stage directory = copy of addons/bmds/ (api/, executors/, data_structures/, README, renovate.json)
- Plus data-structures/ (from 02-backend/demospipes/data-structures/) — the original context addons/bmds/ doesn't contain data-structures (it's at ../../../data-structures = 02-backend/demospipes/data-structures). So add it.
